summary:
Piura has no statute, enforcement record or incident specific to trans visitors in the sources; the national framework of Peru is the whole of what is documented, and it binds Piura as national legislation. Nothing in the record marks Piura as an aggravation of, or a refuge from, that framework, and no local mitigation is documented.

The central mechanism is a national restriction on restroom access. On 20 February 2025 the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved a draft opinion merging bills 6506 and 8457, introduced by Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Muñante, which bars trans people from public restrooms that do not correspond to their birth sex. Exceptions cover custody, cases where medical attention is required, and accompanying an elderly person, a child under 12 or a person with disabilities, and the draft bans 'ambiguous' bathroom signage. The measure was prompted by a July 2023 social-media complaint about gendered restroom labels at Jorge Chávez airport, and stood at committee stage in February 2025.

On 2 April 2025 the congressional Plenary approved the bill and exempted it from a second vote. Its article 5 bars any person from entering or using a public sanitary service that does not correspond to their 'biological sex', with narrow listed exceptions. The April 2025 Law that Strengthens the Right to Sexual Integrity of Children and Adolescents carries that requirement into force, including for trans youth, and the same legislative package bans inclusive signage such as 'women in their diversity'. The law governs Piura as national law.

The legal analysis of IDEHPUCP by Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte holds that the provision violates the equal-treatment and non-discrimination principle of article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights. Its stated aim of preventing child sexual abuse, they argue, rests on a stigmatising stereotype that implicitly presents trans people as likely restroom harassers, while UN reporting shows trans people are more often victims than aggressors. LGBTI activist Gianna Camacho adds that bathroom access would come to depend on the personal judgment of security staff, including identity-document checks, and states that there is no record of sexual assault by trans women in women's restrooms.

Hate-crime protection for LGBT people is absent from the Penal Code. Peru's Congress voted in 2017 to strip those provisions, with Popular Force and Alliance for Progress members carrying the repeal after an April Constitutional Committee vote and amid a petition claiming one million signatures. The result leaves Peru one of only three countries in South America, alongside Paraguay and Guyana, without LGBT anti-discrimination coverage in hate-crime law.

Violence against trans people is documented and under-recorded. A 2024 report found hate crimes rising in the country with trans women most affected, and its co-author Gianna Camacho, a trans journalist and human-rights defender, stated that the recorded figures are only a sub-registry. Between 2020 and 2023, 54 transgender and gender-diverse people were killed, trans women most affected.

In December 2025 three police officers, Dino Ponce, Luis Quispe and Juan León, were sentenced to 17 years' imprisonment for the rape and torture of Azul Rojas Marín, a trans woman and LGBTI activist, nearly 20 years after the attack and after years of litigation. It was the country's first conviction in a case motivated by sexual discrimination and, per BBC News Mundo, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights' first torture-by-discrimination case in the region's history; the case reached the Court through the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights.

Enforcement of the restriction reaches private as well as public settings. A consumer-protection body dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against a gym that enforced the policy. On television, presenter Ana María Salcedo of Willax TV publicly harassed Susel Paredes, the first openly lesbian member of Congress, telling her to 'go use the men's room'.
tangentialFactors:
The Inter-American Court of Human Rights held in Advisory Opinion OC-24/17 that gender identity falls under protected personal autonomy and that states must guarantee trans people's full rights, placing the domestic restroom regime in tension with the region's binding human-rights standard. IDEHPUCP has recorded dehumanising comparisons made on the floor of Congress by congressman Lizarzaburu in the course of the same debate.

Speech and association are also constrained. Vague child-protection articles in the April 2025 law, including an article 4 ban on media and advertising content, enable censorship of identity, artistic and educational material, and the minimum sentence for obscenity was raised from three to four years. Human Rights Watch states that child protection is a pretext for repression and the scapegoating of trans people.
localsOnly:
Two protective developments are on record for residents. In June 2024 the country's health authorities removed outdated pathologising terminology for gender diversity from official health guidance, described as a step toward dignity for trans patients in healthcare settings. In July 2025 a Lima constitutional court, after an activist legal challenge, ruled an anti-equality decree unconstitutional.

Residents of Piura remain without local protective machinery: no municipal ordinance, local police protocol or regional health measure extending protection to trans people is documented, and hate-crime law provides no LGBT anti-discrimination coverage. Trans residents are subject to the same national restroom restriction and the same enforcement environment in private businesses as visitors.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Piura-specific statute, enforcement action, complaint outcome or documented incident involving a trans person appears in the sources; the absence of such material is unresolved rather than evidence of a different local situation. The direction of local enforcement, including whether Piura police or municipal authorities apply the bathroom provision actively, is not sourced.

No entry, visa, identity-document marker or border-screening rule affecting trans travellers is recorded in this inventory, so the position on documents at entry to Peru and on screening at Piura's airport remains unsourced. The scope of the exceptions listed in the bathroom bills, and how front-line staff are instructed to apply them, is not specified in the sources.

The recorded homicide figures for 2020 to 2023 are described by their own co-author as a sub-registry, so the true scale of violence is unresolved. Whether the gym complaint dismissal, the televised harassment of Susel Paredes or the congressional statements produced any sanction is not sourced.
